subject: Performance qualification — handoff & prompt sets
messages:
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana White <dana@acmeretail.com>, Acme Retail Eng Team <eng@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance qualification — handoff & prompt sets

Hi Dana / Acme Eng,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on the use case and expected UX. Quick recap and the asks from our side so we can scope the benchmark run: 

What we heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Target UX: streaming first-token latency is important (users should see partial output within the first 1s for longer generations).
- Latency SLOs: you indicated wanting sub-400ms p95 for typical prompts, with tighter p50 expectations for short interactions.
- Throughput: initial project expects ~30–50 sustained requests/sec during peak batch runs.
- Concurrency: production concurrency expected to be in the 8–16 concurrent "live" sessions range.
- Streaming: required. Partial-token streaming + support for resumable prompts (KV cache reuse) is valuable.

From Redwood — what we propose to measure and the artifacts we need from you:
1) Measurement targets to validate: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latencies (both first-token and final-token), sustained throughput (reqs/sec), and end-to-end session concurrency behavior.
2) Reproducibility: we run against a pinned model revision + prompt set you provide. Please attach a canonical prompt set (we can accept the text file you mentioned).
3) Harness: we will execute the benchmark via our harness (link to our public README below) and will provide raw token-level timings and aggregated percentiles.
4) Test modes: quick smoke (hosted, shared pool) vs isolated Dedicated run. For repeatable SLO validation we recommend Dedicated for the initial pass.

Next steps / asks for Acme: 
- Please send the prompt set you want us to use (anonymize or mask any PII). We received an initial draft during the call; attaching a placeholder expecting your final.
- Confirm the latency targets we should validate (I captured p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms as your comfortable range — confirm).
- Confirm preferred test window (we can run Dec 10–12) and whether you want the Dedicated isolation.

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (placeholder from our call), slo_summary_table.csv (template for us to fill). Also linking the harness docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/blob/main/README.md

If that looks good I will loop in Laura (benchmark lead) and propose a test plan.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
--

From: Dana White <dana@acmeretail.com>
To: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Retail Eng Team <eng@acmeretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance qualification — handoff & prompt sets

Karthik — thanks for the write-up and apologies for the delay. All looks good; a few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed targets (updated after internal sync):
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for the first-user-visible token on short prompts (<= 128 tokens). For longer generations we prioritize early partial outputs within 1s and final p95 <= 800ms for 300–500 token responses.
- Throughput: sustained 40 req/s for our peak traffic profile (we will run a separate stress set at 60 req/s to understand headroom).
- Concurrency: nominal 8 concurrent live sessions; stress runs at 16 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: yes — we need chunked streaming with first-token and periodic flush every ~32 tokens.

We can provide the canonical prompt set (we've finalized it and masked customer PII). Uploading the file now as acme_prompt_set_v1_final.txt — please use this exact set for runs. We also attached a short doc describing behavioral acceptance criteria (sensitivity to partial outputs, stop-sequence fidelity).

One ask: we prefer the Dedicated run for the primary validation (to remove noisy neighbors). If cost is an issue, we can do a smoke run on Hosted first.

Preferred test window: Dec 11 (Fri) morning PT — ideally start 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm the time zone for your scheduling.

Dana White
Director, AI Platform
Acme Retail
--
Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1_final.txt (text file, 122KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dana White <dana@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance qualification — handoff & prompt sets

Hi Dana — great, thanks for the prompt set and the clarity on targets. Im Laura (Im leading the bench runs for this engagement). Below is a concise benchmark methodology and the artifacts we will deliver. Please review and flag any gaps.

Benchmark methodology (proposed):
1) Definitions / measurement points
   - First-token latency: timestamp(request received by the server) -> timestamp(first byte of user-visible token emitted to client). We will report p50/p90/p95/p99.
   - Final-token latency: request->last token emitted. Report same percentiles plus distribution by prompt length bucket (<=128, 129-300, 301-600).
   - Throughput: completed requests/sec over steady-state windows (60s windows for aggregation).
   - Concurrency: number of simultaneous in-flight sessions measured by our harness; we will run controlled ramps to 8 and 16 concurrent sessions.

2) Reproducibility & environment
   - Model pinning: we will pin an exact model artifact SHA and config (quantization/precision flags) and provide that metadata.
   - Warm-up: each run will have a deterministic warm-up phase (50 requests) to populate KV caches before measurement phase.
   - Seeds & RNG: harness will disable nondeterministic sampling seeds for latency runs; for quality sampling runs we will set fixed seeds and report seed values.
   - Logs: raw token-level timestamps (CSV), server-side GPU metrics (nvidia-smi samples), and system-level metrics (CPU, mem).

3) Test plan & schedule
   - Dry smoke (hosted): quick verification on Dec 10 to sanity-check scripts — 30m.
   - Dedicated run (recommended): Dec 11, 10:00 AM PT — 3 x 20m measurement buckets: baseline (8 concurrency), stress (16 concurrency), throughput sweep (30/40/60 req/s).
   - Follow-up: we will share a results package within 48 hours of the run with artifacts + a short assessment doc with recommended optimizations (batching, cache hints, quantization profile).

4) Deliverables
   - Raw CSV: token-level events and request-level summaries.
   - Aggregates: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency tables, throughput curves, CPU/GPU utilization graphs.
   - Repro script: exact harness commands, model pin, and env vars to reproduce the run.

Attachments & links: benchmark_instructions_v1.pdf (detailed checklist), harness README (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/blob/main/README.md).

Logistics / confirmation items for Acme:
- Confirm the Dec 11 10:00 AM PT window and that youll approve Dedicated for an isolated run. If Dedicated is approved, provide any IP allowlist entries we need for the test agents.
- Confirm whether you want us to capture user-visible partial outputs (we can include a short video capture for UX review).

If all good Ill book the Dedicated slot and share the run commands and expected runtime.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Performance & Evals Lead
Redwood Inference
--

Laura / Karthik — confirmed. We approve a Dedicated run on Dec 11 at 10:00 AM PT. A few operational notes from our side before you schedule: 

- Prompt set: uploaded final set (acme_prompt_set_v1_final.txt) — tokens per prompt range 100-450; please preserve ordering for the acceptance buckets.
- Masking: PII fields have been replaced with <MASK> tokens; we consent to sharing masked prompts and accept recording of partial outputs for UX review.
- Allowlist: our infra team will add Redwood test agent IPs to the allowlist (Ill send the CIDR block separately).
- Capacity & budget: we have a dedicated credit allocation for this qualification. If you need >3 hours of Dedicated time let us know before the run.
- NDA / approvals: I signed the DocuSign NDA you sent this morning (link: https://app.docusign.com/XYZ-nda-4521).

Please proceed to schedule the Dedicated slot and share the exact run command and the model pin prior to starting so we can record the start event in our change log. Looking forward to the results.

Thanks,
Dana White
Director, AI Platform
Acme Retail
